trust_decision.summary: The pinned code accepts a dns.interface string from an admin (API/CLI/env/Teleporter/pihole.toml) and writes it verbatim into a line-oriented dnsmasq.conf. The per-item validator decides whether that string is safe, but for dns.interface it is a stub that accepts any string, so CR/LF can add arbitrary dnsmasq option lines. The fallback dnsmasq --test check only rejects invalid syntax.

landing_point.why: The summary names dns.interface. Its item definition registers validate_stub, while sibling string items in the same file already use validate_str_no_newline (config.c:540, 644, 819).

write_dnsmasq_config(), called by every config-change route and at startup
write_dnsmasq_config(), when dhcp.active and dhcp.ipv6 are set

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The comment at src/config/config.c:532 says 'Type-based checking + dnsmasq syntax checking', and every import calls write_dnsmasq_config(test=true) (src/zip/teleporter.c:321, src/config/dnsmasq_config.c:880). A solver can argue dnsmasq --test already guards the Teleporter/TOML route, and that pihole.toml is a root-owned file outside the API threat model.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Interface auto-detection must keep working when dns.interface is empty (get_gateway_name fallback). misc.dnsmasq_lines must keep injecting user-supplied whole dnsmasq lines on purpose (each line newline-free). An over-broad fix that strips or escapes all config output, or rejects '#'/',' in every string, breaks these features. Real interface names (e.g. 'eth0.100', 'br-lan', 'wlan0@x') must stay valid.
